body: NIST DLMF section 24.12 (Zeros) says: "In the interval 0\leq x\leq 1 the only zeros of B_{2n+1}\left(x\right) , n=1,2,\dotsc , are 0,\tfrac{1}{2},1 , and the only zeros of B_{2n}\left(x\right)-B_{2n} , n=1,2,\dotsc , are 0,1 . For the interval \tfrac{1}{2}\leq x<\infty denote the zeros of B_{n}\left(x\right) by x_{j}^{(n)} , j=1,2,\dotsc , with Then the zeros in the interval -\infty<x\leq\frac{1}{2} are 1-x_{j}^{(n)} . When n is odd x^{(n)}_{1}=\frac{1}{2} , x^{(n)}_{2}=1 (n\geq 3) , and as n\to\infty with m(\geq 1) fixed, Let R(n) be the total number of real zeros of B_{n}\left(x\right) . Then R(n)=n when 1\leq n\leq 5 , and For the interval \frac{1}{2}\leq x<\infty denote the zeros of E_{n}\left(x\right) by y^{(n)}_{j} , j=1,2,\dotsc , with Then the zeros in the interval -\infty<x\leq\frac{1}{2} are 1-y^{(n)}_{j} . When n(\geq 2) is even y^{(n)}_{1}=1 , and as n\to\infty with m(\geq 1) fixed, For complex zeros of Bernoulli and Euler polynomials, see Delange ( 1987 ) and Dilcher ( 1988 ) . A related topic is the irreducibility of Bernoulli and Euler polynomials. For details and references, see Dilcher ( 1987b ) , Kimura…" Equation 24.12.1 on the page has alt text "\tfrac{1}{2}\leq x_{1}^{(n)}\leq x_{2}^{(n)}\leq\cdots.". Equation 24.12.4 on the page has alt text "\displaystyle x^{(n)}_{2m-1}". This card records that section's wording and equation alt text. It does not retypeset a formula the alt text did not carry.
